Senior figures within European football are working out whether there are legal options to oppose Gianni Infantino’s plan to to set up a private company to run Fifa’s competitions, while some executives have privately spoken of their countries being ready to boycott the World Cup.

They are among the more furious reactions to Fifa’s announcements on Tuesday, but others were reminded of another aspect of this long story.

Back when Infantino first started to really ingratiate himself with the US president, advisors within American politics were warning about how integrating yourself with Donald Trump normally goes one way. There’s eventually a will for the wider family to be involved.

open image in gallery Infantino would be set for a potentially lucrative ‘commissioner’ role in the new Fifa enterprise ( Getty )

In any event, we now have a situation where this Fifa are willing to sell off parts of the most precious prize in football - the global good that is the World Cup - to the Trump empire. Josh Kushner, the brother of Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner, is in discussions to be a lead investor in Infantino’s absurd new plan.

Sepp Blatter was willing to go further in his description of all this.

It should be stressed that it is wrong to be too revisionist about the disgraced former Fifa president given that this world wouldn’t be possible without him, but his experience has inevitably given him an eye for the intricacies of the game’s politics.

“The close relationship between the Fifa president and the US president has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football,” Blatter posted.

That’s a huge part of this dismal story summed up - but far from all of it.

It is nevertheless instructive that “the Kushner element” was said to be infuriating many stakeholders “more than the money”.

Where else was Infantino’s relationship with Trump going? Does this not tie in with all the claims that Infantino now sees himself as some kind of tech mogul-style founder, as much as the Pope of football?

Some believe that the six weeks of the World Cup saw him descend too deep into the bubble, to the point we get this, and a point that could bring a bursting moment.

Because, if so much of this has evolved out of Infantino’s shameless obsequiousness with Trump, it has also raised multiple other tensions - right up to the future of Fifa’s not-for-profit status under Swiss law when they are essentially converting their primary asset to a private business entity.

For now, most remain infuriated by the sheer brazenness of Infantino using his position to sell off the World Cup like this.

It was this base emotion that prompted Andy Burnham to comment on it.

Politicos have pointed out that it sets up the new UK prime minister’s first indirect clash with the Trumps, but it’s a point of principle for an authentic football fan like Burnham, and one that will gather popular support.

It’s also the first time since the Super League that the game has seen such a direct major government intervention, which points to the story's scale.

open image in gallery Josh Kushner, the brother of Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner, has been in talks about becoming lead investor ( Reuters )

Burnham’s input may only increase pressure on the Football Association and other federations.

The immediate response from such bodies, like with so many involving Infantino of late, was silence. But on Wednesday morning, the FA expressed “deep concern” over the plans. “When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will make our views clear, and comment further,” a spokesperson added.

All of this has been viewed as especially pertinent for the FA since they have been cast as one of the few European federations edging close to Infantino due to the will to host the 2035 Women’s World Cup and a men’s tournament in 2038 or 2042. Same old, same old.

Despite that, none of them - right up to the FA’s Fifa vice-president Debbie Hewitt - knew about any of this until the media reports. The FA’s statement confirmed that they were blindsided and “completely unaware” of the proposals until Tuesday night.

Now, there is a pressure on virtually all of them to speak up, another tension: The federations are supposed to represent the interests of their football communities above all else.

And the bottom line is now this: there is not a single football fan that wants the World Cup to be privatised, let alone in circumstances such as these. It demands public comment from the national associations as to whether they are in favour or not.

open image in gallery There was a lack of criticism from national associations over issues such as ticket prices and Fifa’s at the World Cup ( AP Photo/Matt Rourke )

This points to a core truth of this story.

The major European football countries of England, Spain, Germany and France could kill this at a stroke, by simply flexing their muscle.

Will they have the nerve, or the courage?

There’s of course an irony in how these are the same countries who offer one misused justification for Fifa’s plans, in how they attract most of the game’s wealth.

For all of Infantino’s appeals to redistribution, though, it’s easy to see how this will evolve in the long term.

There will actually be less money, not more, for the wider game since there will be a financial incentive to maximise the most commercially appealing elements. In other words, the major clubs and the interests of bodies like the European Football Clubs (EFC).

Why would anything else happen if it is now just a business?

EFC, headed by Qatar’s Nasser Al Khelaifi, also occupy an intriguing place in this given that they are trying to run competitions with both Uefa and Fifa.

open image in gallery Uefa president Alexander Ceferin and Nasser Al Khelaifi, of Qatar, PSG and the EFC, are both major figures in how the opposition or support to Fifa could form ( PA )

One partnership is admittedly much deeper than the other. Uefa - to give them their due - have led the way with another strong statement, but many see an irony and political opportunism there since they arguably started this path. They restructured control of the Champions League so it's now partly run with the big clubs - through the EFC - via a commercial enterprise.

Figures within both bodies were nevertheless adamant that the leaderships were already exploring ways - both legal and political - to “front up” and challenge Infantino.

By the same token, Fifa gave clubs $355m for the participation of players at the 2026 World Cup. Are the EFC really going to accept such a comparatively small percentage of competition revenues, if the World Cup is part privatised?

Lawyer Antoine Duval meanwhile pointed to how Fifa’s commercial practices are currently tolerated under EU competition law because they contribute to fulfilling public interests. That drastically changes with such a private dimension, where a considerable aim is increasing value for shareholders.

And, in such a scenario, how sustainable is Fifa’s not-for-profit status under Swiss law?

Even from a purely business perspective, though, there is a huge pertinent question.

What rational or financial argument can there be for Fifa selling off ownership of the most valuable “products” on the planet, something that they themselves would insist is only going to increase in value?

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

It’s not like they’re Barcelona or Real Madrid looking to meet Financial Fair Play restrictions, under a mountain of debt, and against huge competition, where selling off your identity and your future was objectionable as it was.

It’s why this is so much worse.

Fifa don’t need to raise this money. They don’t need to trade off parts of the future.

Other forces are keenly watching, from capitalist interests to autocratic states, especially as they seek to wrest control of the game from western Europe.

It is one of many reasons Uefa are now at the centre of this, as one of many tensions at play.

Except, one of the moments when Infantino feels most tension himself is when fans boo him; when there are banners, when there are protests.

It bursts the bubble he’s in, even if it’s brief.

But now he won’t really experience that until perhaps the 2030 World Cup - and who knows what the complexion of the competition will be like by then.

News.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor to give evidence in trial of man accused of threatening him
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor will give evidence against the man accused of threatening him near his Sandringham home.

Alex Jenkinson, 39, allegedly accosted the former prince, 66, on 6 May.

Andrew was walking the late Queen Elizabeth’s corgis in King’s Lynn, Norfolk, at the time.

The charge says that Jenkinson “used towards Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour with intent to cause that person to believe that immediate unlawful violence would be used against him by any person, or to provoke the immediate use of unlawful violence by him whereby that person was likely to believe that such violence would be used, or it was likely that such violence would be provoked”.

Jenkinson faces a second like charge, relating to a man named Stephen Terry, in the same location the day before.

A one-day trial will take place on 21 December, Chief Magistrate Paul Goldspring said on Wednesday.

open image in gallery Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, formerly Prince Andrew, pictured in 2022 ( AFP/Getty )

Andrew is due to give evidence at the trial via video-link.

Two other witnesses for the prosecution are also due to give evidence.

Jenkinson was detained under the Mental Health Act for around a month in the immediate aftermath of the alleged incident, and he was then given temporary accommodation in a Travelodge.

The court heard he underwent a psychiatric assessment on Tuesday, and a report is due to be prepared for early August.

At Wednesday’s hearing, the court heard that online searches on Jenkinson’s phone are expected to form part of the evidence at trial.

The full details of the searches were not revealed, other than one involving the words “Prince Andrew” and “birthday”, and in written submissions defence barrister Claire Howell said a police officer has prepared a 341-page download of the phone.

open image in gallery Andrew now lives in Marsh Farm on the Sandringham Estate in Norfolk ( PA Wire )

An officer has “conducted keyword searches of the internet browsing history on the download”, and prepared evidence “purporting to exhibit the various downloads which she titled ‘Andrew’, ‘search Sandringham’ and ‘weapons’”.

Jenkinson’s lawyers objected to the way the phone evidence had been prepared, and the court heard an expert forensic police officer is now expected to deliver the evidence for the trial.

Jenkinson, who was not at Wednesday’s hearing, has pleaded guilty to failing to provide a specimen of blood while in custody on May 6.

He denies two charges of using threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour with intent to cause fear of or provoke unlawful violence.

He is on bail on the condition he does not contact Andrew or Mr Terry, enter Norfolk, or go near the royal residences in Sandringham, Balmoral, Windsor, Highgrove or Buckingham Palace.

open image in gallery Andrew was stripped of his titles and evicted from Royal Lodge over allegations about his links to Epstein ( AFP/Getty )

Andrew himself was arrested in March on suspicion of misconduct in public office over his connections with paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein. He was later released under investigation.

Andrew, who became the first senior royal in modern history to be arrested, is accused of sharing sensitive information with Epstein while serving as the UK’s trade envoy.

The former duke was detained on his 66th birthday following allegations that he shared reports of official visits to Hong Kong, Vietnam and Singapore with Epstein.

He has vehemently denied any wrongdoing over his Epstein links.

Andrew moved to Marsh Farm on the Sandringham estate earlier this year after his older brother, King Charles, evicted him from Royal Lodge in Windsor.

Gianni Infantino has told the heads of Fifa’s 211 member associations that they could miss out on a $30m payment if they do not back his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup, and has given them just 53 days to decide.

On Tuesday, Fifa revealed plans to create a new subsidiary to manage the commercial rights and delivery of the World Cup and other major tournaments, with Infantino confirming that the new company - ‘Fifa Forward Enterprises (FFE)’ - would be open to external capital investment.

Infantino’s plans have been heavily criticised by Uefa, who accused Fifa of looking to sell the game’s “soul”, while The Independent understands the threat of a boycott is being discussed by senior European figures. The proposals, though, only require a majority vote, of above 50 per cent, from the 211 Fifa members as well as backing from the Fifa Council.

open image in gallery Infantino is planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors ( PA )

In a letter to the member associations, seen by The Independent, Infantino has promised that national federations would benefit from an increase of its ‘Fifa Forward’ funding from around $8m to $20m for the upcoming four-year cycle between 2027 and 2031 if the new FFE subsidiary is created.

Additionally, the letter states that a “one-off” payment of another $20m would be made available for member associations who vote for Infantino’s proposals on 19 September. In the letter, member associations are then warned that their funding for the 2027-2031 cycle would only stand at $10m if the vote does not pass, meaning they would miss out on $30m.

The member associations were also informed, via Fifa’s press release, that they could expect further increases in future cycles, rising to $24m by 2035 to 2038. Thrive Eternal, led Joshua Kushner, the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, are set to lead the new investment, which Fifa said could raise $4.2bn.

Many of the world’s smaller countries are more dependent on funding from Fifa to run their national teams, develop long-term grassroots projects and and invest in infrastructure, like pitches, academies and stadiums. Before this year’s World Cup, Infantino claimed that “without Fifa, there would be no football in 150 countries in the world”.

Infantino used that claim to justify Fifa’s ticket prices for this World Cup, saying that increase tournament revenues would led to more investment in football around the world. Infantino is seeking reelection as Fifa president ahead of the 2027-2031 cycle and has said that Fifa will explore the possibility of increasing the size of the World Cup to 64 teams.

open image in gallery Infantino is working with figures close to the US president Donald Trump ( PA Wire )

Uefa is set to hold an emergency with its 55 member associations this week and the FA expressed its “deep concern” after it was blindsided by Fifa’s proposals. Concacaf, football’s governing body for North America, has also criticised the plans, but Infantino has many allies across the African, South American, and Asian federations.

An FA spokeswoman said: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

News.title: I’ve found the best EA Sports FC 27 pre-order deals in the UK
News.content:
Football fans, rejoice. There’s a new EA Sports FC 27 game on the way, and it will finally introduce an open game mode to the franchise for the first time.

Borrowing from rival basketball game NBA 2K's The City, the new open world mode is called The Grounds. EA describes it as a “social playground”, where players can create their own footballer, explore different districts and have a kick about in casual or competitive matches.

FC 27 launches on 25 September, and you’ll get seven days of early access from 18 September for anyone who pre-orders the Ultimate Edition or the new Ultimate Plus Edition of the game. Here's everything you need to know about FC 27, including the best pre-order deals.

Best ‘EA Sports FC 27’ pre-order deals

‘FC 27’ Ultimate Plus Edition using EA Play: Was £139.99, now £125.99, Playstation.com

Was £139.99, now £125.99, Playstation.com ‘FC 27’ Standard Edition, PS5: Was £69.99, now £62.99, Amazon.co.uk

Was £69.99, now £62.99, Amazon.co.uk ‘FC 27’ Standard Edition, Xbox Series X/S: Was £69.99, now £62.99, Amazon.co.uk

‘EA Sports FC 27’: What’s new?

open image in gallery ( EA Sports )

EA Sports FC 27 seems to stick to EA’s well-trodden formula. As with many iterations of EA’s beloved game, it’s a fairly iterative version of the game you know and love.

The biggest new feature is The Grounds. EA calls it a social playground. You’ll be able to create your own footballer and freely explore a series of football-themed districts, meet up with friends in The Grounds, challenge others to casual or competitive games, complete skill-based activities and earn rewards as you develop your character. Fans have been clamouring for a shared social hub for years, so it’s nice to see it finally coming to the game.

EA also says that it has improved how dribbling, passing, shooting, defending and its goalkeeper AI work to make matches feel more responsive and realistic. As with FC 26, players can choose between two gameplay presets. Competitive is designed for Ultimate Team and Clubs, while Authentic slows down the pace of the game and tweaks player behaviour to better reflect real-world football in Career Mode.

Speaking of Career Mode. EA has partnered with TransferRoom, the real-world transfer marketplace that’s used by hundreds of professional clubs, to make Career Mode even more realistic. The transfer system has been designed so clubs now compete more naturally for players, with negotiations changing and adapting over time. Deals are also influenced by a player's ambitions, wage demands and club interest. EA is also introducing new live scenarios based on real football storylines, letting players experience the same managerial challenges that actual football managers face during the season.

Lastly, Ultimate Team. EA is rolling out a new FUT Gallery – a permanent collection of your biggest achievements in Ultimate Team. It will include special player items, trophies and other milestones. There are also new Live Events, as well as a refreshed progression system and additional tournament formats so you can earn rewards throughout the year in different ways. Clubs will also gain new progression features and social improvements.

‘EA Sports FC 27’, Ultimate Plus Edition

open image in gallery ( EA Sports )

EA has launched a new Ultimate Plus Edition aimed squarely at dedicated Ultimate Team players, though it's only available until 31 August.

As with the Ultimate Edition, you'll get up to seven days of early access from 18 September, an untradeable 85+ International Icon Player Item, an additional Football Ultimate Team Player Evolution slot, a range of Career Mode bonuses, The Grounds cosmetic items and bonus content for EA Sports FC 26.

The exclusive bonuses for the Ultimate Plus Edition include 10,000 FC Points delivered over five monthly drops, Premium Passes for Seasons 1 to 5, a Hall of FUT Player Pick featuring five former stars and a Physical Evolution that boosts any player's physical attributes to 99 in FC 26.

Just by pre-ordering, you'll also get a range of Career Mode bonuses, including three Icons or Heroes, a Dynamic OVR Pre-Season Boost, a five-star coach, five-star youth scout, five-star senior scout and five additional Manager Live Challenge creation slots. ‘EA Sports FC 27’, Ultimate Edition

open image in gallery ( EA Sports )

Wimbledon achieved record attendance and generated nearly 5 billion social media "impressions", the All England Club announced on Wednesday, despite competition from the football World Cup.

A cumulative 550,151 fans passed through the gates during the fortnight, slightly up on the figures recorded for last year’s tournament, with many purchasing tickets on the day via Wimbledon's famous queue.

Daily attendance records were also set on three separate days during the championships.

Organisers credited these bumper figures to the first rain-free Wimbledon since 2019 and the unexpected semi-final run of British wildcard Arthur Fery, which helped offset potential viewer losses to the World Cup.

Fery defied the odds to pick up notable wins over the likes of Grigor Dimitrov and Flavio Cobolli as he reached the last four before eventually losing to French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

The German star was subsequently beaten in four sets by Jannik Sinner in the final as the world No 1 retained his title following his 2025 triumph over Carlos Alcaraz.

open image in gallery Wimbledon was on at the same time as the men's World Cup (Martin Rickett/PA) ( PA Wire )

The tournament's commercial appeal was evident in retail figures, with a record 117,995 hats sold across the fortnight. Broadcasting numbers were also high, with ESPN reporting it was the second-most-viewed Wimbledon championships of all time. The tournament's social media following grew by 11% across all platforms.

The all-Czech women's singles final between Linda Noskova and Karolina Muchova proved particularly popular in the Czech Republic, where Eurosport sub-licensed coverage to free-to-air broadcaster Prima. The match attracted a 38.5% audience share and peaked at 900,000 viewers.

The attendance figures are particularly impressive given England’s deep run at the World Cup, which saw Thomas Tuchel’s men reach the semi-finals.

The Three Lions topped their group before achieving knockout wins over the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mexico and Norway.

However, England ultimately failed to end 60 years of hurt as they suffered a 2-1 defeat by Argentina in the semi-finals.

England did manage to pick themselves back up to beat France 6-4 in a thrilling encounter three days later, as they secured a third-place finish, their best placing since the 1966 tournament on home soil.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at the 2018 Commonwealth Games in Australia and was selected again for this summer’s Games in Glasgow.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

News.title: Europe faces energy crisis as gas stockpiles sink
News.content:
Britons face a winter of surging energy bills as Europe struggles to secure enough gas to fill its storage tanks.

A squeeze on Qatari gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European gas stockpiles into “energy crisis territory”, analysts at Wood Mackenzie warned.

The Continent’s storage tanks are barely 50pc full, a historical low for this time of year. Fresh tension between the US and Iran has cut the chances of more tankers sailing anytime soon.

Wood Mackenzie now forecasts that Europe will enter the winter with its gas storage tanks no more than 75pc full, compared with a five-year average of 90pc.

This could drive up prices, as Europe competes with Asia to buy extra gas, mostly from America on the spot market.

“Europe is approaching energy crisis territory,” Wood Mackenzie warned on Monday.

Meanwhile, Britain, which no longer stores significant amounts of gas, faces paying even more than rival buyers.

“The UK’s market model is that we’ll always pay more than anyone else, rather than relying on storage,” said David Lewis, an energy analyst at Wood Mackenzie.

“If other markets are going to struggle, it just means that the UK price will be even higher.”

Last week British Gas boss Chris O’Shea warned the country risked shortages over winter because of low levels of storage.

European gas prices fell at the fastest pace in a month on Monday after a pause in attacks between the US and Iran over the weekend, dropping to about €58 per megawatt hour.

Goldman Sachs expects the price to remain at about this level for the next three months, which is 80pc higher than the pre-war price of €32.

But the US investment bank warned the price could hit €100 next year if Middle East energy exports were slow to get back to normal.

The pressure from lost Qatari supply is being compounded by the EU’s plan to prohibit imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) from next year.

This will leave Europe in a bidding war with Japan and China for US LNG supplies.

Britain produces half its own gas and imports the rest, mostly via pipeline from Norway. But the Norwegian gas will largely track global LNG prices.

Laura Page, of the analysis firm Kpler, said Britain’s heavy reliance on Norway left it perilously exposed to any supply interruption.

“If there was a pipeline outage in Norway, or a problem with the gas field, that could cause prices to increase,” she said.

Mr Lewis said the Norwegians were postponing as much maintenance on their gas rigs as possible, to keep the supply flowing for Europe’s depleted stockpiles.

“But the problem is the same as in the UK: these are mature fields, they require a lot of maintenance, a lot of careful management,” he said.

Goldman Sachs said Europe had “only small room for error” in its gas stockpiling, and capacity could be as low as 28pc by the winter’s end.

Mr Lewis said the Netherlands and Germany were particularly exposed. “They might struggle to actually deliver the gas during peak demand days,” he said.

The El Nino weather pattern that will prevail for the rest of this year might come to Europe’s aid, delivering a milder winter than usual.

“It’s going to be an expensive winter unless we have a mild winter, which is what everybody’s hoping for at the moment. Fingers crossed,” Mr Lewis said.

Sports.title: ‘No one has the right’ – Sepp Blatter joins condemnation of Fifa successor Gianni Infantino over World Cup sale plans
Sports.content:
FORMER Fifa president Sepp Blatter has slammed Gianni Infantino’s decision to try and sell off the World Cup.

On Tuesday it emerged that controversial footie chief Infantino was planning to create a company to own the World Cup and Club World Cup.



Then he would be able to auction off shares to private investors and earn millions in the process.

The news has caused widespread outrage with the FA and Uefa among the bodies to hit back.



And now, Infantino’s predecessor Blatter – who lost his role due to Fifa‘s corruption scandal in the mid-2010s – has given his thoughts.

Writing on X, Blatter, 90, said: “The close relationship between the Fifa President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football.



“No one has the right to sell our game.”

A leaked letter from Infantino to the 211 Fifa associations says that they will make £30million if his outlandish scheme goes through.

Countries have less than two months to sign up with a £10billion package “available as of January 1, 2027.”

But the reaction from some of the sport’s big dogs has not been good.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The FA said: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

Central and North America‘s suits added: “We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.



“We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game.

“Collectively, Fifa, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport.

“Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

“This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the Fifa family will act in the same manner.”



Why 'dictator' Infantino's shameful plot to sell World Cup is destined to succeed By Simon Collings GIANNI INFANTINO sent shockwaves through football with his latest plan to change the game as we know it. The controversial president, for his part, can point to the huge revenues Fifa have generated since his time at the helm over the past ten years to explain his popularity. And if this shameful scheme is to get the green light, it will require the majority support of Fifa’s 211 member associations and the governing body’s Council. There are a few reasons – well, actually, a million or so reasons – why they could be on board with them. Read this article in full…

Uefa fumed: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. Uefa takes it extremely seriously.

“So should every National Football Association.

“So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially.

“None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa’s to sell.”

Sports.title: World Cup buyer Joshua Kushner is worth £3.9bn, has Victoria’s Secret model wife, Trump family ties & dad who was jailed
Sports.content:
FIFA’S bombshell plot to sell the World Cup to private investors has got football fans fretting over who might end up calling the shots.

The governing body insists it will retain majority control over the tournament – but there are concerns around the influence investors will have as they push for a return on their cash.



Even more worrying for many supporters are the ties the proposed investment group has with Donald Trump.

Fifa chief Gianni Infantino has spent the last few years cosying up to the US president.



But flogging portions of the World Cup to a group spearheaded by Joshua Kushner – the brother of Trump’s son-in-law – kicks things up a notch.

Fifa has confirmed that Thrive Capital – the investment firm launched by Kushner in 2009, when he was just 24 – will lead the group through the purchasing process.



Other figures close to the Trump administration are understood to be involved, too.

Infantino has told Fifa members they will receive £30million each if they back his plan in the next 53 days, according to The Times.

The FA and Concacaf say they are “deeply concerned” about the proposal, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also condemned.

So, naturally, football fans are now wondering, who are the people involved? Who is this business hotshot Joshua Kushner who could become one of the most influential figures in the sport?



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Kushner name is well-known in the States.

The family has made a fortune in real estate and politics, with dad Charles and brother Jared both landing prominent roles in the Trump regime.

Charles, 72, who served 14 months behind bars after being convicted of illegal campaign contributions, tax evasion and witness tampering, before being pardoned by Trump in 2020, was appointed the US ambassador to France and Monaco last year.

Jared, 45, is America’s special envoy for peace, which involves working on diplomatic relations mainly in the Middle East and Russia. He is also married to Trump’s eldest daughter, Ivanka.



Joshua, 41, is known in the business world as “the other Kushner”. He keeps a lower profile than Charles and Jared but is said to have a close relationship with his older brother.

Both studied at Harvard University and have tried their luck with a handful of joint business ventures since graduating.

Jared was actually an investor in Thrive Capital but was forced to offload his stake before taking a White House job in 2017.

Despite success being well distributed throughout the family, prospective World Cup buyer Joshua has made the most cash.

His tech company was among the early backers of Instagram and OpenAI, and now manages a whopping £18.6BILLION worth of assets.



That has left Joshua with a healthy £3.9bn personal fortune.

It is perhaps no surprise, then, that he mixes in elite circles.

He married entrepreneur, supermodel and former Victoria’s Secret Angel Karlie Kloss in 2018.



They have three kids, split their time between sprawling residences in Miami and New York, and have acquired a handful of recognisable media brands through their joint-venture Bedford Media.

The loved-up couple are good pals with Taylor Swift and were spotted at her and Travis Kelce‘s wedding earlier this month.

Kushner is also well-connected in the sports industry, having bought minority stakes in basketball franchise the Miami Heat and MLB team the San Francisco Giants.

Now he has his sights set on the World Cup.

The Kushner family is deeply embedded in the White House but Joshua has distanced himself from the Trump administration.



He is actually a lifelong Democrat, as is wife Karlie, who says she has never met Trump.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Karlie publicly supported presidential bids from Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, who all ran against Trump.

Kushner did not vote from Trump in 2016 and attended the Women’s March in Washington D.C. shortly after his inauguration.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish trains with Spanish second division side after missing out on Man City pre-season squad
Sports.content:
JACK GREALISH has been training at a second division Spanish club after being left out of Manchester City’s pre-season squad.

The attacker spent last year on loan at Everton but is yet to seal a transfer this summer.



Grealish, 30, looks set for another move away from the Etihad Stadium after falling down the pecking order.

The former Aston Villa captain was left out of the club’s pre-season squad for the tour of Hong Kong and Seoul.



He had reported for duty last week but was not picked for the 30-man group by Maresca.

Grealish has made sure to keep up his fitness during the transfer window by jetting off for some warm-weather training.



He has settled into training at RCD Mallorca’s training ground in Spain as revealed in an Instagram story.

Grealish posted a video of himself on the pitch at the venue with the caption “Working”.

Sports.title: Infantino offers to pay Fifa member countries £30m EACH to agree to World Cup sale plot as bombshell letter is leaked
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO has told Fifa member associations they will receive £30million if they agree to his plan to sell off the World Cup.

The Fifa chief’s hopes to allow private investment to purchase chunks of the World Cup through a sister company, Fifa Forward Enterprise, were revealed on Tuesday.



And now The Times report that the official has told the 211 associations that make up Fifa that they will have 53 days to sign up to the plan to receive their considerable sums.

A leaked letter has laid bare the financial incentives for member associations should private investment be allowed to purchase stakes in football‘s biggest competition.



As part of the communication, Infantino told members a funding package of $10billlion (£7.5m) will be made available should members sign up to his plans, compared to a package of $2.7b (£2b) if they do not.

The letter read: “The decision on whether or not to proceed with this proposal belongs entirely to you.

“Should you wish to proceed this $10b package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together.

“Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme [development money] of $2.7b as previously presented.

“In total for the upcoming cycle starting as of January 1, 2027 each member association will have the possibility of access up to $40m per member association under this proposal.”

The proposals revealed on Tuesday would see a new sister company created to oversee the World Cup, in which shares could be purchased by private investment.

Infantino himself stands to earn considerable sums in bonuses should the proposal come to pass.

And he could even take up the role as “commissioner” of the new body following the end of his Fifa term in 2031 – a role which could see him net tens of millions more.

A number of organising bodies have come out against the plans, with the FA releasing a statement calling the lack of transparency “deeply concerning.”

The statement read: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.



“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

Those sentiments were echoed by Uefa, the governing body for international football in Europe, who released a statement slamming Fifa for trying to trade the soul of the sport.

The release read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. Uefa takes it extremely seriously.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade – especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not Fifa’s to sell.”



Sky Sports reported that European nations are weighing up a BOYCOTT of the World Cup should the proposal go through.

Concacaf, who manage international football in North and Central America, shared their “deep concern” over the lack of transparency involved in the plans, and the apparent lack of oversight involved in their creation.

The body wrote: “Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release. We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, Fifa, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport.

Sports.title: What Chelsea do with NINE strikers fighting to be Pedro’s understudy including controversial new forward ‘up for sale’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have spent years trying to solve their No9 problem – now Xabi Alonso has NINE options to deal with.

When Danny Welbeck joins on a surprise two-year deal from Brighton, the Blues will be overflowing with strikers.



Joao Pedro asserted himself as the club’s out-and-out centre forward last season and will surely be first choice again in year two at Stamford Bridge.

But who Alonso settles on to fill his squad for a campaign without European football remains to be seen.



He is certainly spoilt for choice. So here’s who is in contention – and who isn’t.

Danny Welbeck

Chelsea have been crying out for some experience in the squad since BlueCo’s 2022 takeover. Now they will have some.



Welbeck is an ideal backup in a three-man attack. Someone to take the midweek cup matches and occasional low-key Prem fixture.

He will raise standards in training, has been extremely durable in recent seasons on the south coast, and is something different to others.

Olivier Giroud was the last player Chelsea had in this mould – and he became a cult legend.

Welbeck might not do that, but at least he won’t be able to score AGAINST Chelsea anymore.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Verdict: Keep.

Liam Delap

The Englishman was the worst of three strikers who played against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday in a first televised pre-season friendly.

He has had a stinker since joining for what looked a good price at £30million last summer.

But Delap has been more of an unwanted battering ram up front, making fouls and taking his frustration out on opponents.



He may well want to stay at SW6 (who wouldn’t, on a long, big contract?) but he has the least to offer right now.

Verdict: Sell.

Emmanuel Emegha

Nobody knows how much Chelsea paid sister club RC Strasbourg for their captain. It was a transfer completed a year ago and caused outrage.

At the time, Dutchman Emegha was coming off a strong season in Ligue 1 – 14 goals and three assists in 27 games – but he’s hardly played since.

Hated by his own fans in France after announcing an exit as captain, Emegha is a controversial figure and has already been bumped down the pecking order at Chelsea.



But he may well have more to offer than Delap, so it is a shootout between him and Nicolas Jackson for who takes the second choice spot behind Joao Pedro.

Surely Chelsea won’t sell him before he’s played a competitive game, though. That makes a loan and a possible sale next year more likely.

Reports suggest the club will listen to offers. His injury forcing him to miss the start of pre-season has been horribly timed.



It keeps up an unwanted fitness record which could concern Alonso.

Verdict: Loan.

Nicolas Jackson

On paper, Jackson is definitely the second best option of the lot.

But he’s also the most valuable player who the club would be happy to shift.

With a not unreasonable pricetag of £65million, a serious profit is there to be made.



Jackson is wanted by Aston Villa and might fancy his chances of being a regular starter in a reunion with former Villarreal boss Unai Emery.

The prospect of him linking up with Cole Palmer again, and maybe even Joao Pedro dropping deeper, is certainly appealing, though.

Joao Pedro, Jackson, and Welbeck covers all bases. But if Jackson wants to pursue his career elsewhere, Chelsea won’t stop him.

Verdict: Keep.



Dastan Satpayev

The big winner of Alonso’s tour Down Under opener is this Kazakhstan wonderkid.

Still only 17 – and not officially even a Chelsea player until his birthday next month – the £3.5million trialist has made quite the splash.

He will need time before being Prem ready, but with a year of adult football – and some Champions League action as well as senior international games – under his belt, Satpayev might be further along than many imagined.

Staying in the academy is unlikely to test him. But regular minutes will be needed.



The alternative is to keep him around to acclimatise and settle in England, perhaps with the view of promoting him fully next summer.

Verdict: Loan.

Marc Guiu

After two years of mismanagement and not enough pitch time, Guiu is a goner.

Chelsea would love to get £25million for the Barcelona La Masia graduate, but that will be a stretch.



If he went away to Ligue 1, Belgium, or Holland and bagged a load of goals, it would be an easier sale.

Like the rest of this list, he isn’t away on pre-season, so isn’t going to be hanging around.

Verdict: Loan.

Shumaira Mheuka

The lack of call-up to Alonso’s travelling party speaks volumes for Shim Mheuka.



Not because he’s not good enough – he really is, and don’t back against him being a bolter for England’s 2030 World Cup group either – but because he is being lined up for a loan.

The 18-year-old is dominant at PL2 level so getting the right move for him this season is vital.

Chelsea have to get it spot on if they are to help their Under-21 captain realise his enormous full potential.

Verdict: Loan.



David Datro Fofana

Most fans have probably forgotten – or wish they had – that Fofana ever played for Chelsea.

Fofana has had a host of underwhelming and outright disastrous loans. It’s time to cut ties permanently for everyone’s benefit.

Chelsea only spent £10million on him in January 2023. Profit, even a small one, shouldn’t be hard to come by.

Verdict: Sell.



Deivid Washington

File this one next to DDF under: Chelsea still own him?

Washington cost a dumb £17million in Todd Boehly‘s sporting director summer of 2022.

He has barely played any football since.



Chelsea sent him back to boyhood club Santos on loan last year and it did not go well.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Somehow they need to get him off the books.

Verdict: Sell.

Sports.title: Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made
Sports.content:
Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made

Liverpool are targeting PSG winger Bradley Barcola this summer, and their chances of a deal have been boosted by former Reds forward Luis Diaz

View 2 Images Former Liverpool forward Luis Diaz has made a decision over his future (Image: David Ramos, Getty Images)

Bayern Munich winger Luis Diaz may have provided a boost to Liverpool's hopes of signing Bradley Barcola this summer. The Reds have been heavily linked with the PSG forward as they continue their search for a Mohamed Salah replacement.

‌



Salah left Anfield at the end of the season, leaving Liverpool searching for a way to replace his goals and assists. Barcola seems to be the player who has come out as the number one target, although a deal is expected to cost over £100 million.

‌



Our sister title The Liverpool ECHO reports that it is unlikely to put Andoni Iraola's side off making a move. They do, however, face competition from both Bayern Munich and Arsenal, and this is where Diaz comes in.

‌

The Colombian has been a resounding success at the Allianz Arena since completing a £66million switch from Liverpool last summer. During his debut season in Germany, he netted 26 goals and laid on 23 assists across 51 appearances in all competitions.

That impressive form has attracted attention from Saudi outfit Al-Hilal. French publication L'Equipe claimed that the club were preparing to table an opening bid of at least €70million (£60m) for the wide man.

‌



However, Sky Germany reports that Diaz has informed Bayern that he wishes to remain at the club. The German champions are therefore unwilling to enter into negotiations with any club regarding a potential transfer, and have not placed an asking price on Diaz.

The 29-year-old still has three years left to run on his contract at the club. With Diaz's future appearing to be settled, this should bring Bayern's pursuit of Barcola to a close. With all of their attacking options remaining in place, they are unlikely to venture into the transfer market to bolster that area of their squad.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is emerging as a key transfer target for Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal are also said to be prioritising a move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior over Barcola. This could potentially leave Liverpool with a clear path to the PSG star.

The French club may have been more receptive to a transfer amid their pursuit of RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, who had also attracted Liverpool's attention. They have, however, been pipped to the post by Real Madrid.

PSG have since taken the remarkable step of issuing a statement confirming they have withdrawn from the race for the Ivory Coast international. "PSG has this evening officially withdrawn its interest and its bids for Yan Diomande," the statement read.

‌



"The asking transfer fee and salary demands were completely disproportionate and distortive - and PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance.

"As a two-time consecutive Champions League winner and the most successful club in recent years, PSG will also not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents - and will instead calmly and confidently continue its transfer planning."

Sports.title: Ranking Man Utd's four transfer priorities as exit set to change Michael Carrick's plans
Sports.content:
Four signings down, four to go? Manchester United have spent £85million this summer, bringing in two centre midfielders - Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans - and two goalkeepers - Karl Darlow and Kit Margetson.

And while United still want to strengthen one of those positions, they have other priorities. Michael Carrick was able to stick with a tight squad last season, often going more than seven days without a fixture thanks to the Red Devils being out of the both domestic cups by the time he took over.

But this season, United's return to the Champions League calls for more depth. That's why club chiefs want to bolster Carrick's options all over the pitch.

Midfield has long been the top priority, but with Santos and Tielemans through the door, and striker Joshua Zirkzee in talks to join Juventus on loan with a £30million option to buy, things have changed.

‌



With that in mind, Mirror Football is here to rank United's four transfer priorities.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd eye TWO strikers with Joshua Zirkzee closing in on transfer exit READ MORE :

Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery READ MORE :

Striker

Although Joshua Zirkzee only started one game under Carrick - after United had secured Champions League football - there's no doubt that his departure would leave a hole in the squad. The Dutchman played second fiddle to Benjamin Sesko last term and was needed in the final knockings of the campaign after Sesko picked up an injury which has also ruled him out of pre-season so far.

Zirkzee has started both of United's friendlies, scoring one goal and providing one assist, and is expected to lead the line again on Saturday against Atletico Madrid - unless he's in Italy sealing a move. Juventus are the frontrunners to sign him, with Roma and Como also interested.

‌



His impending exit should prompt United into the market for a replacement. Aston Villa's Ollie Watkins was of interest last summer while ex-Juventus striker Dusan Vlahovic is available on a free transfer.

Or should the Red Devils look outside the box? Ivan Toney scored 55 goals in Saudi Arabia last season and is proven in the Premier League, and prior to Chelsea's swoop, Danny Welbeck would've been an option.

Which position should Manchester United prioritise? Have your say in the comments section.

View 4 Images Manchester United would need a replacement for Joshua Zirkzee (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

‌



Centre midfield

Bumped down to second place from our last set of rankings, United have since addressed their previous top priority. It became even more important to sign at least two midfielders when, after Casemiro had left on a free transfer, Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup, ruling him out of much of the new season.

But given that Santos, Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo are the only fit senior centre midfielders in Carrick's squad, another wouldn't go a miss. Aurelien Tchouameni is understood to be United's No.1 target and the ex-Monaco star could be allowed to leave Real Madrid if they sign Rodri from Manchester City.

Roma's Manu Kone has also been shortlisted alongside Bournemouth youngster Alex Scott. However, United are unlikely to make a bid for Scott, with Chelsea having seen a £64m offer rejected by Chelsea.

View 4 Images Aurelien Tchouameni is a target for Manchester United (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Left-back

To the defence now and despite Luke Shaw managing to start all 38 Premier League games last season for the first time in his career, his fitness will always remain a concern. Shaw, 31, remains susceptible to injury and playing every few days would likely be too much.

Patrick Dorgu has developed into more of a left winger and with United open to selling Harry Amass, it's clear that they'd like to bring in a new left-back. Newcastle's Lewis Hall is understood to be on their radar and reportedly open to a move to Old Trafford.

But given that Newcastle have already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali - and are in advanced talks with Arsenal over Bruno Guimaraes - it may well be impossible to sign Hall for a reasonable price. Fulham defender Antonee Robinson is an alternative.

View 4 Images Lewis Hall is keen to join Manchester United, according to reports (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



Left wing

If Barcelona had triggered their option to sign Marcus Rashford for just £26m, signing a left winger would've been higher on United's to-do list. But with Rashford back in the fold, it makes things complicated.

There seems to be no active escape route for the England international right now and he's set to return to training in the coming weeks to work under Carrick for the second time. But things can change, and United are open to selling Rashford for around £40m.

Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye is admired by the Red Devils and said to be open to a transfer amid interest from Al-Hilal. Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo has also been touted, a lesser-known name who would be a cheaper option to serve as backup to Matheus Cunha.

But bringing in a player of Vinicius' calibre and profile would take their summer business to a completely different level and send a clear message to their Premier League rivals.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool move 'agreed', Vinicius Jr to Arsenal, Marcus Rashford swap
Sports.content:
The latest transfer news from Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and more as they look to improve their teams ahead of the Premier League season

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Wednesday, July 29th.

There is little over a month remaining of the transfer window as clubs continue their preparations for the new season. Already, two deals worth more than £100million have been completed, with Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea from Aston Villa and Elliot Anderson making the switch from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City.

They may not yet prove to be the biggest deals of the summer. Vinicius Junior's future at Real Madrid remains unresolved, and Arsenal are willing to move for the Brazilian if the opportunity arises.

The Gunners are prepared to offer the star the biggest deal in their history, but also want to improve in other areas. Their interest in Bruno Guimaraes is still causing plenty of drama as Newcastle deny any suggestion of advanced talks for the midfielder.

Liverpool are still looking to delve into the market, with new boss Andoni Iraola keen to land a winger. Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola remains of interest.

Manchester United have already landed two midfielders, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, in recent weeks but could still add another. The futures of Marcus Rashford and striker Joshua Zirkzee could still lie away from Old Trafford.

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposal could trigger £51m Man Utd transfer
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford swap deal proposal could trigger £51m Man Utd transfer

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford is set to return to the club, with his future uncertain, but Old Trafford chiefs may have the opportunity to offload the academy product

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could be used in a swap deal (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester United could use Marcus Rashford in a bid to land Roma star Manu Kone. The Red Devils are looking to continue their midfield reinforcement push, and the Frenchman has been the subject of their interest.

‌



United have so far been unwilling to meet Roma's £51million asking price, but Gazzetta dello Sport in Italy suggest that Rashford could provide a suitable makeweight to get a deal over the line. Kone is poised to leave the Stadio Olimpico this summer as the Italian look to fund their own transfer plans and adhere to Financial Fair Play regulations.

‌



Roma have fielded multiple enquiries regarding the Frenchman, but neither United nor Al Ahli have been convinced by that valuation. Reports claim that Michael Carrick's side could take advantage of Roma's desire to sign a left-sided forward.

‌



However, the England international's wages would present difficulties for the Italians. They would require United to foot up a significant portion of Rashford's salary for a loan arrangement.

United chiefs prefer a permanent exit for Rashford after his loan spells to Barcelona and Aston Villa both ended without a move being made permanent. A successful stint at Camp Nou did not even get a deal over the line.

Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

The Catalan outfit declined to sign Rashford permanently despite possessing an option to acquire the 28-year-old for £26m. They opted instead to recruit Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United.

‌



No club has yet met United's asking price for Rashford, while reports suggest the academy graduate turned down the prospect of a move to Turkey. As it stands, Rashford looks set to return to Old Trafford.

The forward has not featured for the club since December 2024, but still has two years left to run on his contract. A clause that would have permitted him to leave for £40m - to any club other than Liverpool or Manchester City - has now expired.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is set to return to Manchester United for the moment (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rashford remains United's highest earner, pocketing £325,000 per week and accounting for a considerable chunk of the club's wage bill. While the board will be eager to shed that financial burden, Michael Carrick indicated at the end of last season that he was open to the idea of the forward staying put.

"Whoever's here, I want to work with, and help them improve," Carrick said. "At the moment, it's this squad of players. There's obviously players on loan, and whatever happens with that later on will happen.

Article continues below

"But certainly, as a coach, and leader of a squad, we want to get the best out of everyone."

Sports.title: Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks
Sports.content:
Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) have been approached by a consortium led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia over buying a minority stake in the club

View 2 Images Jeff Bezos has been approached over investing in Liverpool (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group remain in talks with a consortium interested in buying a minority stake in Liverpool, the club's chief executive Billy Hogan has confirmed.

‌



FSG released a statement last week saying that Amit Bhatia had expressed an interest in buying a stake in Liverpool. The British-Indian businessman was the director and co-owner at QPR for 18 seasons and has the backing of the the Mittal family, who are worth £26bn, according to Forbes.

‌



Despite being the son-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal, who leads ArcelorMittal, the globe's biggest steel and mining firm, Bhatia has reportedly approached Jeff Bezos about joining his consortium. The Amazon founder, the fourth-richest man in the world with a net worth of over £190bn, is said to be considering the prospect.

‌



Asked for an update on the situation, Hogan told Bloomberg: "I can only refer back to the statement from FSG last week that we have been approached by a consortium that's led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia for a strategic minority investment in the club. And I wouldn't say anything than that at this point."

Liverpool star confirms Mo Salah contact as true impact of star's exit made clear READ MORE :

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 when they were on the verge of administration for £300m and, according to the Financial Times, the potential deal being outlined by Bhatia would value the club at £4.5bn. They previously sold a single-figure stake to global sports investment firm Dynasty Equity in 2023 and are now weighing up another deal.

This deal is understood to only be at the preliminary stages, but is for a much more significant stake, potentially 30 per cent of the club.

‌



Bezos has previously been credited with an interest in buying NFL franchises, with the Washington Commanders and Seattle Seahawks on his radar. Neither has materialised thus far and the Amazon billionaire's investment would be much smaller if he did become involved with Liverpool.

View 2 Images Amit Bhatia is leading the consortium (Image: Andrew Fosker/REX/Shutterstock)

Liverpool have won the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup and Carabao Cup since FSG's arrival 16 years ago, but are entering a period of flux. Andoni Iraola has arrived to replace Arne Slot following a disappointing 2025/26 season, while Michael Edwards left his role as FSG's chief executive of football earlier this month.

Article continues below

Edwards joined Liverpool in 2011 and was promoted to sporting director in 2016 before leaving in the summer of 2022. His departure is a significant blow to FSG and Liverpool while there has also been speculation over the future of Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes.

Sports.title: Arsenal told Real Madrid have 'obligation to sell' Vinicius Jr as Spanish media back transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal told Real Madrid have 'obligation to sell' Vinicius Jr as Spanish media back transfer

Arsenal have been linked with Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior and media in Spain have backed the blockbuster transfer

View 3 Images Vinicius Junior has been linked with a colossal transfer to Arsenal (Image: Getty)

Spanish media believe Vinicius Junior could still join Arsenal this transfer window. This is despite widespread reports suggesting the Real Madrid and Brazil star will stay put.

‌



The Gunners head into the new season as defending Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years and have looked to sharpen their attack. Christos Tzolis has already been signed from Belgian side Club Brugge for £34million, but Mikel Arteta seemingly wants more.

‌



Last week, news surfaced that Arsenal were exploring a move to sign Vinicius Junior, which would likely be the window's headline transfer. However, more recent updates suggest he is keen to remain at the Bernabeu and pen fresh terms, with his current deal set to expire in 2027.

‌



Irrespective of the suggestion that Vinicius won't be going anywhere, some outlets in Spain reckon that his club have an "obligation" to sell him and that there could be more to this narrative than meets the eye.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr has already promised to join club as Arsenal handed transfer timeline READ MORE :

Ex-Real Madrid goalkeeper Santi Canizares spoke on COPE's Tiempo de Juego programme about the Vinicius saga and thinks that his former side would rather sell their star than see him leave for free next summer.

‌



View 3 Images Vinicius's current contract expires in 2027 (Image: Getty)

"The more noise there is about a player, the less chance he has of leaving," he stated. "[But] Real Madrid are late with everything. If it's true that he doesn't have a signed agreement, Real Madrid have an obligation to sell him. You can't lose 100 or 100-plus million euros by letting a player's contract expire. I just don't believe it's going to happen. It's an unforgivable mismanagement."

The fee many reports claim Vinicius would cost this summer is in the £100m-plus range. But with the likes of Sky Sports News reporting that he will stay and that Real Madrid have zero interest in selling him, it could be that a new deal is signed rather than a groundbreaking transfer sanctioned.

‌



However, one Spanish outlet hints that there hasn't been a meeting about renewing Vinicius's contract for some time and suggests there could be more to come regarding the 26-year-old's future. Deputy director of AS, Tomas Roncero, states: "The club says there probably won't be a problem, because he intends to renew.

"If you talk to Vini's people, they tell you that his only wish is to stay at Madrid and leaving isn't even on his mind. But curiously, there hasn't been a single meeting for eight or nine months. The last time, there was a huge financial disagreement, because his demand was to earn the same as Kylian Mbappe. Madrid made it clear to him that he's not going to earn the same as Mbappe.

"There will be no agreement on those initial terms. I'd like to think that Vinicius will lower his financial demands, which would also be reasonable. You have to understand the pecking order within a club and it's clear that Real Madrid's star player is Mbappe.

‌



View 3 Images One Spanish outlet thinks wages could become an issue because of Kylian Mbappe (Image: Getty)

"He's the all-time leading goalscorer in World Cup history, World Cup Golden Boot winner, Champions League Golden Boot winner, and La Liga top scorer. His individual statistics speak for themselves. And Vini hasn't been quite as outstanding. He has to understand that he can't earn the same amount."

On Vinicius potentially leaving for free, he added: "Real Madrid want to avoid that scenario. The Yan Diomande deal is a clear message that Vinicius might not stay. Otherwise, there wouldn't be such urgency to spend 120 million euros on a 19-year-old player. Such a big gamble only makes sense if you're also covering your back."

Article continues below

Roncero's colleague and chief editor of AS, Aritz Gabilondo, also stated: "If both sides want to renew, the deal is signed and that's it. Someone here is playing a different game.

"It’s a strategy that Real Madrid – and specifically its president – has historically taken a dim view of. Taking a gamble on Florentino Pérez in this instance is very tricky."

Sports.title: FA 'deeply concerned' as they issue statement on FIFA's plan to sell off World Cup
Sports.content:
FA 'deeply concerned' as they issue statement on FIFA's plan to sell off World Cup

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under fire amid plans to sell shares in the World Cup, sparking anger from fans and confederations such as UEFA, who have accused him of 'crossing a line'

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino wants private investors in the World Cup (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

The Football Association have released a statement saying that it is 'deeply concerned' by Gianni Infantino's plans to sell off the World Cup. FIFA announced on Tuesday - after reports leaked its plans - that it intended to expand 'football development funding' to more than $10billion (£7.5bn) by inviting third-party investment to its competitions, including the World Cup.

‌



It has been claimed that Infantino could make millions from private investors. European confederation UEFA issued a strongly-worded statement accusing FIFA of 'crossing the line', while the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that FIFA had 'sold out'.

‌



Now the FA have spoken out in a statement published on Wednesday which read: "We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

‌



"Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved. When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gary Lineker shows FIFA disgust in four-word response to Gianni Infantino bombshell READ MORE :

UEFA nations could BOYCOTT World Cup in light of FIFA's plot to sell tournament READ MORE :

Alongside UEFA, CONCACAF - the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football - have joined the criticism. "CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release," it began.

‌



"We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process. We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

"As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, Fifa, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

"This is the framework within which CONCACAF operates. We trust that all within the Fifa family will act in the same manner."

‌



Should the confederations break away from FIFA? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images UEFA attacked FIFA in a strongly-worded statement (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

UEFA will hold emergency talks on Wednesday and could discuss breaking away from FIFA competitions in what would be a drastic move. "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," the European body said.

‌



"UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."
